# cboxdk/telemetry-native

An optional PHP extension (`cbox_telemetry`) that measures the PHP runtime:
statistical CPU profiling, native operation timing, runtime counters and a
signal-safe crash recorder. Companion to cboxdk/laravel-telemetry, which owns
all semantics, sampling policy, redaction and export. No Laravel knowledge, no
networking, no policy in the C.

PHP 8.3–8.5, NTS only. Linux (glibc and musl) is the production target; macOS is
development-only and samples wall clock rather than CPU time. MIT licensed,
clean-room — nothing taken from Excimer (GPL-2.0).

## Documentation

- [docs/index.md](docs/index.md): overview, the three-layer mental model, section TOC.
- [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md): install, read a first profile, tail retention in one page.

- [docs/getting-started/testing.md](docs/getting-started/testing.md): testing code that must work with and without the extension.
- [docs/core-concepts/architecture.md](docs/core-concepts/architecture.md): unit of work, the five functions, the rules the C holds itself to.
- [docs/core-concepts/profiler.md](docs/core-concepts/profiler.md): the safe-point stack walk, frame interning, trie aggregation, reading the output.
- [docs/core-concepts/operations.md](docs/core-concepts/operations.md): which calls are hooked, why aggregates rather than records, known limits.
- [docs/core-concepts/crashes.md](docs/core-concepts/crashes.md): breadcrumbs, record contents, signal safety, draining.
- [docs/configuration/reference.md](docs/configuration/reference.md): every INI setting with defaults, bounds and mutability.
- [docs/cookbook/unit-of-work.md](docs/cookbook/unit-of-work.md): the integration pattern and the two ordering mistakes to avoid.
- [docs/security/_index.md](docs/security/_index.md): what is collected, what is refused, crash sink protection.
- [docs/decisions/0001-operation-hook-mechanism.md](docs/decisions/0001-operation-hook-mechanism.md): why handler swaps beat the Zend Observer, with benchmark numbers.
- [docs/decisions/0002-timer-backends.md](docs/decisions/0002-timer-backends.md): why not SIGPROF, and why macOS uses a timer thread.
